intro: Sagole is a village in the Vhembe district of Limpopo, in the far north of South Africa, east of Tshipise. Near it stands the Sagole Baobab, a Champion Tree and the largest baobab in the country, with a trunk almost eleven metres across and limbs as thick as tree trunks spreading over a bare earth yard. Its Venda names include Muri kunguluwa, the tree that roars. A reader sent us their photograph of it in leaf.

trees.story:
The Sagole Baobab is the largest baobab in South Africa, a Champion Tree with a trunk 10.8 metres across and 32.89 metres round, according to Wikipedia. It stands east of Tshipise in the Vhembe district of Limpopo, near the village of Sagole, and its Venda names include Muri kunguluwa, the tree that roars. It became the stoutest tree in the country after two other large baobabs, at Glencoe and Sunland, collapsed in 2009 and 2016.

A reader sent their photograph with a GPS fix taken at the tree, about a kilometre from the point Wikipedia gives, and an age of about 1,200 years, which is their estimate. The photograph shows the tree in leaf, and it is less a trunk than a landscape. Grey limbs as thick as tree trunks leave the base and run out sideways, one of them bending down to rest near the ground before rising again, and the crown spreads over a bare earth yard. Two visitors stand beside that long, low limb and look small against it.

Wikipedia gives the tree 20.5 metres of height and a crown 38.2 metres across, and notes that mottled spinetails, a kind of swift, breed in it. It also records an entrance fee to see the tree.
